headline: Fed hike odds near 77 percent after the payrolls beat put Tuesday's US CPI at center stage
subhead: The S&P 500 rose 0.3 percent to 7,376.9 and the 10-year yield to 4.86 percent on Friday, while WTI ended the week down 12.8 percent and India holds its Muhurat session today.

us.text: The S&P 500 rose 0.3 percent to 7,376.9 and the Nasdaq 1.1 percent as chipmakers recovered part of Thursday's rout; the Dow fell 0.5 percent.
Futures put a December Fed hike at about 77 percent after October payrolls rose 165,000 and unemployment fell to 4.1 percent.
Next week turns on October CPI on Tuesday, with FactSet's estimate at 3.9 percent year on year, and producer prices on Friday.

india.text: Nifty rose 2.0 percent to 25,030.4 and Sensex closed at 81,028.0 on 6 November, led by M&M, ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank.
Foreign investors bought a net 13,749.8 crore rupees of shares on 6 November and domestic institutions sold 5,968.7 crore, provisional data show.
The rupee gained 52 paise to settle at 93.89 per dollar on 6 November on a weaker dollar and strong equity inflows.

global.text: Kospi fell 6.0 percent to 5,059.7 on 6 November after briefly breaking 5,000, as Samsung fell 6.4 percent on AI regulation fears.
Europe fell on 6 November, with the DAX down 1.9 percent and the FTSE 100 down 1.0 percent on the US tech rout and hot payrolls.
WTI ended at 90.83 dollars, down 12.8 percent on the week, its biggest weekly drop since 2022, on hopes of a US-Iran deal.

weekly.narrative: The US midterms set the tone: a relief rally on Wednesday gave way to Thursday's AI chip rout on fears a Democratic Congress curbs data center building, and Friday's partial rebound and a 165,000 payrolls beat still left the S&P 500 down 2.7 percent and the Nasdaq 3.4 percent on the week. India went the other way, with foreign buying and cheaper crude lifting the Nifty 8.6 percent on the week and above 25,000 on Friday, while Kospi and the Nikkei bore the brunt of the chip selloff. Hopes of an Iran deal drove WTI down 12.8 percent on the week, and gold rose 4.5 percent and silver 5.5 percent despite rising Fed hike bets, while Bitcoin slipped 3.4 percent. Next week brings US CPI on 10 November, India CPI on 12 November, China's rare earth export pause expiring and a reported start to Anthropic's IPO roadshow.
